question.leadin: Answer the following about Southeast Asian independence movements.
question.text: Ho Chi Minh led this nation's independence movement from France, which culminated in its victory at the Battle of Dien Bien Phu. The 1975 Fall of Saigon ended an American war in this country.
question.answerHtml: Vietnam [or Socialist Republic of Vietnam or Cong Hoa Xa Hoi Chu Nghia Viet Nam; prompt on SRV]
question.clue: Rioting against the presence of one of these countries in the other resulted in a coup which created the government in exile GRUNK.

swap.leadin: After a brutal 1975 invasion, this country occupied East Timor until 2002.
swap.text: Name this Asian island nation formerly led by presidents Sukarno and Suharto. The largest Buddhist temple in the world, Borobudur, was built in the 9th century by the residents of this country's island of Java.
swap.clue: This country's capital after it gained independence was Yogyakarta.

question.leadin: There are many large rivers that start out in China or on the Chinese border, but are better known for being elsewhere. Name some of them.
question.text: It starts parallel to the Yangtze River on the Tibetan Plateau and flows south. It then continues through Laos and Cambodia until it cuts across Vietnam and has a delta at Ho Chi Minh City.
question.clue: This Southeast Asian river, rising in China's Qinghai Province and emptying into the South China Sea.

swap.leadin: This site, built by Khmer emperor Suryavarman II, was designed to resemble Mount Meru, the home of the gods in Hinduism.
swap.text: Name this temple complex near the city of Siem Reap, the largest religious structure in the world.
swap.clue: This structure unusually faces west unlike the Bayon to its north and is located near two barays.

question.leadin: A king in this modern-day country apocryphally killed the prince Mingyi Swa in a 1593 duel.
question.text: Name this country where King Naresuan ruled the Kingdom of Ayutthaya. The Chakri dynasty would later take power in this country under the leadership of Rama I.
question.clue: Its rulers used the Paknam Incident to create an irredentist nationalism later deployed by the Phibun government.

swap.leadin: Name the following about Southeast Asia during the colonial period.
swap.text: Led by the Chakri dynasty, this country was the only Southeast Asian country to escape colonization. It lost Laos and the Malay peninsula to the French and British, respectively, and retains its monarchy today.
swap.clue: A king of this country considerably lessened the trade restrictions of the Burney Treaty by agreeing to the Bowring Treaty with Great Britain.

question.text: This first Indonesian president signed the Proclamation of Indonesian Independence. His system of "Guided Democracy" collapsed after a Western-backed coup by his successor, Suharto, overthrew him.
question.clue: This leader hosted the meeting which led to the formation of the Non-Aligned Movement in his country's city of Bandung.

swap.text: This man led the insurgency against Spanish and later American colonists as part of the Katipunan Society, and later was the first President of the Philippines.
swap.clue: Earlier, he quarreled with Andres Bonifacio over divisions in the Katipunan movement.

question.text: This conflict was one of the innumerable things the RAF opposed. American involvement in this conflict began after the Gulf of Tonkin Incident, and its action included the Tet Offensive.
question.clue: The use of Agent Orange to defoliate trees during this conflict was controversial for its health effects on soldiers.

swap.text: This country started exporting rice thanks to efficiencies gained from adopting IR8 rice. This country became a "Tiger Cub" economy during the presidency of Fidel Ramos in the 1990s.
swap.clue: An American occupation of this nation was resisted by the islamic Moro people and revolutionaries led by Emilio Aguinaldo.

question.leadin: This brutal tyrant helped overthrow Lon Nol and ordered the killing of over a million people.
question.text: Name this Cambodian dictator who ruled from 1975 to 1979, when the Vietnamese drove him from power.
question.clue: This leader, who was referred to as "Brother Number One", helped Prince Sihanouk's ("SEE-uh-nook") attempt to return to power after he was deposed in a coup by Lon Nol.

swap.leadin: This party forced urban "New People" to move to the countryside and become "Old People"
swap.text: Name this political party which lost power after an invasion by the Vietnamese in 1979. It was responsible for the murder of thousands of prisoners in its country's "Killing Fields".
swap.clue: This group forced city residents into agricultural communes in the countryside, and turned the Tuol Seng high school into Security Prison 21.

question.text: Commander Dante and Victor Corpus were almost executed along with this man, a longtime friend of members of the NPA. This man's widow took power after the People Power Revolution.

swap.leadin: Answer the following related to the Taungoo ("TOWN-goo") Empire, an early modern state in Southeast Asia.
swap.text: The Taungoo Empire and its successor states, including the Konbaung dynasty, were both based out of this modern-day country later governed from Mandalay by the British.
swap.clue: Lion statues from this country name long-range Chindit brigades.

question.leadin: Answer the following about piracy in the Indian Ocean.
question.text: For defeating pirate Chen Zuyi, who raided ships entering the Indian Ocean, Zheng He ("jung huh") was honored with incense in this city. Seized by Portugal in 1511, this city controlled trade through a nearby waterway of the same name.
question.clue: Control of this city hyperbolically afforded control over Venice according to the Suma Oriental of Tome Pires ("TOH-may PEE-rish"), who spent two years in this city after arriving from Goa.

swap.leadin: This empire is often cited as evidence against August Wittfogel's (VIT-foh-gull's) "hydraulic empire" thesis because its irrigation system was controlled by monks and not the state.
swap.text: Name this empire that built dikes called barays to irrigate its land with water from the Tonle Sap. It was ruled by multiple kings named Jayavarman.
swap.clue: Among the landmarks in its main capital were the temples Ta Prohm, the Baphuon, and Ta Keo, the first of which was made entirely from sandstone.

question.text: This second major important Burmese empire was founded by King Mingyinyo near the end of the Ava dynasty.

swap.leadin: This dictator, who bathed in dolphin blood to stay young, betrayed his ancestry by persecuting ethnic Chinese with the Enterprise Nationalization Law of 1963.
swap.text: Name this autocratic Prime Minister who ruled for 26 years after using the Union Revolutionary Council to seize power in 1962, after which he released an ideological tract titled as his country's "way to socialism."
swap.answerHtml: <u>Ne Win</u> [or U <u>Ne Win</u>; accept Thakin <u>Shu Maung</u>; prompt on “<u>Ne</u>” or “<u>Win</u>” or “<u>Shu</u>” or “<u>Maung</u>”]
swap.clue: Nu was deposed by this general, who infamously replaced Burma's 50- and 100-kyat bills with 45- and 90-kyat bills just because they were divisible by the lucky number nine. The 8888 Uprising toppled this socialist dictator, who notably bathed in dolphins' blood to stay young.

question.leadin: This ruler of the Toungoo dynasty rose to the throne after his brother-in-law Tabinshwehti was assassinated.
question.text: Identify this king who ruled a unified Myanmar from 1551 to 1581, and was notable for his patronage of Buddhism, including the building of pagodas and the distribution of copies of the Tripitaka.

swap.text: This communist group closely allied with the Viet Cong succeeded in ousting the French and the Lao royal family in 1975.
swap.clue: The book Man in the Region of Death was an account of this organization's prison camps by former RLG official Thongthip Rathanavilai, though unlike the Khmer Rouge this organization never established massive death camps.
